  • Constructor Details

    • TwoFluidComponentConservationReport

      public TwoFluidComponentConservationReport(double elapsedTimeSeconds, int acceptedSubsteps, String[] componentNames, double[] initialInventoryKg, double[] finalInventoryKg, double[] inletBoundaryMassKg, double[] outletBoundaryMassKg, double[] inventoryResidualKg, double[] relativeInventoryResidual, double maximumRelativeInventoryResidual, double[][] finalPhaseInventoryKg, double[][] interphaseTransferKg, double maximumInterphaseTransferResidualKg, double[][][] phaseMassFractionProfile, double minimumMassFraction, double maximumMassFraction, double maximumMassFractionSumError, double maximumPhaseMassSynchronizationErrorKg, double interphaseLatentHeatEnergyJ, boolean converged, String message)
      Create an immutable component-conservation snapshot.

      This constructor is public so the component transport implementation in the sibling two-phase-pipe package can publish diagnostics. Callers normally obtain reports from TwoFluidPipe.getLastComponentConservationReport().

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if names or array dimensions are inconsistent, required numeric values are non-finite, or elapsed time/substep count is negative

    • getInterphaseTransferKg

      public double getInterphaseTransferKg(TwoFluidComponentConservationReport.Phase phase, String componentName)
      Get signed interphase transfer accumulated in one phase for a named component.

      Positive values enter the phase. The gas, oil, and water values for each component sum to zero apart from floating-point round-off.

      Parameters:
      phase - phase identity
      componentName - NeqSim component name
      Returns:
      signed transferred mass in kg

    • getInterphaseLatentHeatEnergyJ

      public double getInterphaseLatentHeatEnergyJ()
      Get the latent/compositional heat added to the fluid sensible-energy equation.

      Positive values denote heat released by phase formation; negative values denote heat consumed. Phase-specific partial component enthalpies are evaluated from the cell's conservative named-component slate.

      Returns:
      interval-integrated latent heat in joules
